description: Definitions the screen socket's messages and the HTTP routes share.

Capability.description: Something a connector can do with a device. The viewer and the agent tools offer only what the connector in use can do.

Encoding.description: How screen frames travel: JPEG images, or an H.264 Annex-B stream.

EncodingSetting.description: The encoding a scope asks for. auto is H.264 where the viewer can decode it, JPEG where it cannot.

DeviceState.description: How a device stands: being brought up, streaming and taking input, running but failing to stream, unable to start, or gone.

Share.description: A fraction of the screen: 0 at its left or top edge, 1 at its right or bottom edge.

Screen.description: A device's screen: in points, which touches and snapshots use, and in pixels, which frames use.

Device.description: A running device, as a viewer is told about it.

runtime.description: The runtime as a person says it, such as iOS 26.5.

reason.description: Why the device is stalled, failed or stopped; null otherwise.

since_ms.description: How long the device has been in this state.

viewers.description: How many screen sockets watch the device.

busy.description: What the device is kept for while agents' gestures would get in its way, such as a test run; null otherwise.

booted_by_us.description: Whether SimMirror booted this device, and so may shut it down.

app_hierarchy.description: The app in front sharing its view hierarchy through SimMirror's debug SDK, as an agent's last snapshot read it; null when none does. An older server does not send it.

AppHierarchy.description: An app sharing its view hierarchy through SimMirror's debug SDK, so snapshots read what accessibility leaves out.

name.description: The app's name as the home screen shows it.

sdk_version.description: The version of the SDK the app was built with.

Agent.description: Who is acting on a device: an agent, by a key that stays the same for its connection, and the title a viewer shows.
